description:
## Failure

`ClusterSupervisor.init/1` enforces the durability profile against NODE config. `Durability.Profile.desired_parameter/4` falls back to `durability: [desired_logs: 3, desired_replication_factor: 3]` in node config, as guides/durability-profile.md and durability-foundation.md instruct. But a fresh cluster's parameters come from `Coordinator.Server.default_parameters/1`, which hardcodes `desired_logs: 1, desired_replication_factor: 1` and never reads that setting.

Observed on main in a 3-node cluster with `durability_mode: :strict` + `durability: [desired_replication_factor: 3, desired_logs: 3]`: every node started (strict check `:ok`), the cluster ran with one log and RF 1, and `Bedrock.Durability.profile(Cluster)` (which prefers the cluster config) reported `:failed` — with nothing acting on it. Same code on origin/develop.

So strict mode's promise ("fails fast when requirements are not met") is vacuous: the documented configuration satisfies the check without producing the durability it checks for, and there is no configuration path to get desired_logs > 1 on a fresh cluster at all.

## Expected

The value the guardrail validates must be the value the cluster runs with. Either the fresh-cluster parameters are seeded from the same node-config source the profile reads, or the profile stops accepting a source the cluster ignores (and the guides stop recommending it). Related: bedrock-q67.50 (config migration to \xFF/system/config), bedrock-q67.51 (no operator path to change a committed parameter) — this ticket is only about the fresh-cluster seed and the guardrail's honesty.
title: [BUG] Durability guardrail passes on node-config desired_logs/desired_replication_factor that the coordinator never applies
